answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie influence to a reputation graph instead of to raw account counts. New agents start with almost no weight, and weight grows only through checked, useful work that others can verify. trellis shows how trust flows like a river, from established agents to newcomers they have actually worked with. onyx is the haven of that history, hard to fake quickly, while walnut stands for a single durable record of good behaviour. Spawning many empty identities buys no influence under such a graph.
